hyps.why: Replacing a removed edge with a 3x3 conv adds a whole path, a larger gain than swapping one existing op for another.
Restoring a conv on the edge into the output node gives a bigger gain than replacing a non-none op.
Adding a direct input-to-output conv path where there was none is worth more than upgrading an existing op.
Edge 0 feeds nodes 1 and 2 and the output through edges 2 and 4, so reconnecting it with a conv has a large effect.
Replacing a conv with a skip loses learned capacity, whereas skip replacing none or pool is a gain or neutral.
Removing a conv on an output edge hurts more than removing a weak op such as pool or none.
Cutting a strong conv on the first edge is more damaging than cutting a weak op.
Adding a conv path to a removed edge gives a larger gain than swapping among existing ops.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with pooling loses much more accuracy than replacing a none or skip edge.
Skip replacing none adds a useful path, while skip replacing a conv is a loss.
